title: list_applications_with_pairing bypasses the SP-index single-flight gate and has no gate of its own; two frontend surfaces call it
rationale: On a cold tenant, Home mounting and the operator clicking App Registrations before it returns runs two full `/applications` scans and two `/servicePrincipals` scans (tens of seconds each on a large tenant), and a concurrent gated reader (Enterprise Apps, MI list, search prewarm) runs a third SP scan because `state.single_flight(sp_index_key)` never sees this caller. The same file's sibling helpers were explicitly rewritten to avoid this. The dedicated `sp_index_watch` helper exists only to serve this bypass.
proposal: Replace the `None` arm with `futures::future::try_join(client.list_applications_all(query, Some(APPS_MAX)), cache::sp_index_cached(&state, &client, &tenant_id))` (keeps the concurrency, gains the gate and the correctly-keyed watch; `sp_index_watch` and the `Some(cached_index)` arm become unnecessary since `sp_index_cached` hit-checks). Wrap the miss path in `state.single_flight(&cache_key)` with a post-lock re-check, as `search_corpus` does.
verifier_notes: mod.rs:174-196: the `None` arm calls `client.list_service_principals_index()` directly under `try_join`, bypassing `state.single_flight(sp_index_key)` that `sp_index_cached` holds (cache.rs:242-258); there is also no gate on `apps_pairing_key` itself. cache.rs:352-355 documents that the sibling `indexes_cached` was rewritten to avoid exactly this bypass, and `sp_index_watch` (cache.rs:199-207) exists only to serve this arm. Both frontend callers are real (home_dashboard.rs:38, application_list.rs:234); a Tauri invoke already in flight when the operator switches view keeps running on the backend, so two `/applications` + two `/servicePrincipals` scans plus a third SP scan from any gated reader is the cold-tenant cost. The proposed `try_join(list_applications_all, sp_index_cached)` keeps concurrency (both return GraphError) and inherits the correctly-keyed watch; wrapping the miss path in `single_flight(&cache_key)` mirrors search.rs:120-131. Perf-only, so medium is the ceiling.

title: bulk_remove_expired_credentials walks the whole tenant even for an explicit selection and hardcodes 10_000 instead of APPS_MAX
rationale: The Findings pane's 'Fix all N' and the App Registrations bulk bar always pass `Some(object_ids)` (a handful to a few hundred ids), yet the command still walks every page of `/applications` — tens of seconds on a large tenant — before discarding all but the selection. `ids.contains` is a linear scan per app (10 000 × selection size). And the comment's 'where the cap cannot matter' is wrong: a selected app beyond the 10 000th page position is dropped from `apps`, so `apps_scanned` is short and the UI has no signal (the flag is bound to `_truncated`). The literal `10_000` also duplicates `applications::APPS_MAX`, which audit.rs:84 uses by name.
proposal: When `object_ids` is `Some`, fetch exactly those apps via `batch_get_json::<Application>` on `/applications/{id}?$select=id,appId,displayName,passwordCredentials` (falling back to per-id `get_application` on a whole-batch failure) and skip the list walk; keep the walk only for the `None` tenant sweep. Replace the `10_000` literal with `super::applications::APPS_MAX`. Drop the `HashSet`/O(n·m) and 'dropped selection' points.
verifier_notes: Core premise holds: bulk.rs:163-176 walks `/applications` to the 10_000 cap even when `object_ids` is `Some`, and the only frontend caller always passes `Some(&ids)` (bulk_action_bar.rs:511), so every 'Fix all N' pays a full tenant walk before `retain`. The literal `10_000` duplicates `applications::APPS_MAX` (applications/mod.rs:75), which audit.rs:82, credentials.rs:32 and backup.rs:59 all use by name. `batch_get_json` (batch.rs:88-92) exists and returns per-URL results in order, so fetching the selection by id is feasible. Overstated: (a) `ids.contains` over a few-hundred-id `Vec` against ≤10 000 apps is sub-millisecond — a non-issue; (b) 'silently drop a selected app' requires a tenant with >10 000 app registrations, where the App Registrations list and the audit are already truncated at the same `APPS_MAX`, so the selection could not have come from beyond the cap in the first place; the comment at :157-159 is essentially right. Medium stands for the wall-clock cost on large tenants (the repo's own cache.rs:140-147 comment calls a full re-enumeration 'tens of seconds').

title: Bulk expired-credential sweep busts both tenant-wide indexes (invalidate_app_lists) for a credential-only mutation; the per-app fix uses the tiered invalidation
rationale: applications/cache.rs:140-147 documents why credential mutations must use `invalidate_app_credentials`: it 'deliberately leaves the shared SP pairing index, the app-name search index, the Enterprise Apps list, and every mailbox-scope verdict intact… dropping them forces the next list visit to re-enumerate every app and every service principal (tens of seconds on a large tenant) for a change that touched neither.' `remediate_remove_expired_credentials` (remediation.rs:97-99) follows that rule; the bulk sweep of the same mutation does not, so after every sweep the operator pays a full SP-index + app-name-index rebuild.
proposal: Replace the `invalidate_app_lists` call with a loop over `summaries.iter().filter(|s| !s.removed_key_ids.is_empty())` calling `invalidate_app_credentials(&state.cache, &tenant_id, &s.object_id)` (or add an `invalidate_app_credentials_many(cache, tenant, &[object_id])` that drops the shared keys once and the per-app detail keys per id). Extend `repo_invariants/cache.rs` to pin that no credential-only command calls `invalidate_app_lists`.

No CHANGELOG or doc marks the bulk path as a deliberate exception.

title: Opening the SSO tab runs the SP→app→app-SSO Graph chain twice and reads the SP a third time
rationale: `get_sso_config` is get_service_principal_sso_fields + list_assigned_claims_mapping_policies + find_application_by_app_id + get_application_sso_fields (3-4 serial Graph calls). `get_sso_summary` re-runs all of it just to wrap the same fields in `SamlSsoSummary`/`OidcSsoSummary`, whose extra fields (`saml_summary_urls`, `oidc_summary_urls`) are pure functions of tenant id + app id. The rollover panel then fetches the SP fields a third time. Every SSO tab open is therefore ~8 Graph requests for data the tab already holds, and the summary crosses IPC as an untagged `serde_json::Value` that the frontend re-deserialises and swallows on mismatch.
proposal: Either (a) have `get_sso_config` return the summary (or the `SigningCertRolloverDto`) as fields of `SsoConfigDto`, so one command feeds the whole tab, or (b) build the summary client-side from `SsoConfigDto` + the static URL formulas (move `saml_summary_urls`/`oidc_summary_urls` into `azapptoolkit-dto` so both trees share them). Delete `get_sso_summary` (and its binding) or type it as `#[serde(tag = "protocol")] enum SsoSummary { Saml(..), Oidc(..) }`. Expected effect: ~2x fewer Graph calls per SSO tab open and no double parse.
verifier_notes: sso/mod.rs:1738-1745: get_sso_summary calls get_sso_config again, then only wraps fields plus oidc_summary_urls/saml_summary_urls (pure functions of tenant/app id). get_sso_config = SP fields ∥ claims read, then find_application_by_app_id, then get_application_sso_fields (mod.rs:466-486). None of these reads are cached: get_json's third arg is consistency_eventual, not a cache flag (transport.rs:357-362), and the sso_fields/find_application methods call get_json directly. sso_tab.rs:550-561 fires get_sso_summary only after config resolved (serial), and SigningCertRolloverPanel (73-83) reads the SP a third time. Untagged serde_json::Value round-trip and silent 'Summary unavailable.' on mismatch confirmed at 872-887. Option (a) or (b) is feasible; the URL formulas are already pure helpers.

title: Every mutation rebuilds the whole detail pane and remounts all visited tabs (root cause of the deferred-reload workarounds)
rationale: `bump_reload` re-runs the resource, the Suspend closure yields a brand-new view, and with `Suspense` (not `Transition`; no `<Transition` exists in web-rs) the skeleton flashes first. The keep-alive latch preserves state across tab switches but not across saves, so removing one owner re-runs `list_federated_credentials`, `get_expose_api`, `get_application_authentication`, the Activity audit query + sign-in lookup, the CA list, the Exchange mail-scope lookup and resets the usage panel for every tab that was visited — and discards half-typed forms in other tabs. It also forces the credentials tab's three "defer on_changed until the dialog is dismissed" dances (390-397, 578-584, 600-608) and causes the lost-notes bug in the permissions tab.
proposal: Keep a long-lived `RwSignal<Option<Arc<ApplicationDetail>>>` on the pane, update it from an Effect over the resource (or in the Suspend on success), and mount `DetailHeader` + `TabBar` + the keep-alive tabs once outside the Suspend, passing `Signal<Arc<ApplicationDetail>>` derived from that signal; show `DetailSkeleton` only while the signal is `None`. Tabs then survive `on_changed`, the reveal-dialog deferrals become unnecessary, and per-tab sub-resources only re-run when their inputs change. Interim cheap step: switch `Suspense` to `Transition` to remove the skeleton flash.
verifier_notes: Evidence is accurate: application_detail_pane.rs:129-135 uses `Suspense` (fallback = `DetailSkeleton`), :136-148 rebuilds header, `TabBar` and every `keep_alive` tab inside the `Suspend` on each resource re-run; the `keep_alive` comment (:94-99) explains tab-switch survival only. `grep -rn Transition web-rs/src` returns nothing, so the skeleton flash claim stands. The three credentials-tab deferrals exist at credentials_tab.rs:390-397, 578-584 and 600-608, and the browser test `the_reveal_defers_the_detail_reload_until_it_is_dismissed` (tests/gui/certificate_reveal.rs:279) pins the workaround — the refactor must keep or adapt that test. The long-lived `RwSignal<Option<Arc<ApplicationDetail>>>` + Effect proposal is feasible in Leptos 0.8 and would also remove the root cause of finding 1. Effort L is honest; medium severity fits a refactor whose symptoms are already visible as separate bugs.

Add a `// Source: <url>, reviewed YYYY-MM` comment per constant and note the 2027-02-27 date in docs/DEVELOPMENT.md or the ARM crate header. title: Token endpoint calls have no retry/backoff; the readiness probe fans out six refreshes at once and a 429/5xx surfaces as a terminal `token_exchange`
rationale: AGENTS.md makes `core::http_retry` the one retry budget ("incl. `$batch`"), and every REST client honours `Retry-After`, but the `/token` POST is a single attempt: a 429 from `login.microsoftonline.com` (which does throttle per client/tenant and returns `Retry-After`) or a transient 5xx/network error becomes `TokenExchange("HTTP 429")` → UI `token_exchange` (retryable=true but nothing retries), readiness shows `Unknown` for that half, and a `ScopedTokenAdapter::bearer()` failure aborts the Graph request that needed it. The readiness checklist and the per-audience refresh locks (token_cache.rs:226-229: "Access Readiness fans about six out at once") make simultaneous token requests the normal case, not an edge.
proposal: Wrap the send in `azapptoolkit_core::http_retry::with_retries("aad_token", RetryClass::<idempotent>, |_| async { .. })`, classifying 429 (`Retry-After`), 5xx and `reqwest` transport errors as `Attempt::Retry` and everything else as `Done`. A `refresh_token` grant is idempotent (Entra does not revoke on use), so retrying is safe; an `authorization_code` exchange is single-use, so restrict retries there to transport errors before a response was received. Add a wiremock test: first 429 with `Retry-After: 1`, then 200 → token cached, exactly two requests.
verifier_notes: Evidence real: mod.rs:154-202 is a single `send()`; no `retry` anywhere in the auth crate; `http_retry::is_retryable_code` covers only throttled/server_error/network_error, and graph transport.rs:495-498 fetches the bearer ONCE outside `with_retries` ('A 401 is non-retryable and surfaces to the caller'), so a client's retry budget never covers a transient token failure. readiness.rs:62-66 fans probes out concurrently as described. Concrete cost beyond readiness: `restore_session` at launch on a transient network blip → `Ok(None)` (commands/auth.rs:39-43) → the operator must redo the full browser sign-in although the keyring token is fine. The proposal's split (retry refresh_token grants; only transport errors for the single-use authorization_code exchange) is correct.

title: Grant read-through cache is attached to the per-SP appRoleAssignments read; the tenant-wide appRoleAssignedTo read it describes is uncached
rationale: The comment, the cache-key name (`assigned_to:`) and the stated motivation (audit + consent lens paying for the same full-tenant scan twice) all describe `appRoleAssignedTo` on the Microsoft Graph SP — but both real callers (`prefetch_graph_app_roles` in audit.rs:957 and the consent scan in consent.rs:197) call `list_app_role_assigned_to`, which has no cache. `appRoleAssignments` (what one SP holds) is a small per-SP list that is cheap to re-read; caching it instead brings a 60-minute staleness window to the pre-write `existing` reads in permissions.rs:666 / sharepoint.rs:307 for no measurable win. The only test that touches the key (`deleting_a_service_principal_drops_the_grant_matrices`) seeds `grants:assigned_to:sp-1` by hand, so nothing proves which method writes it. caching-and-search.md ('Page size is a wall-clock divisor') names this read as the one that dominates the audit and consent view, so the intended win is currently not realized.
proposal: Move the read-through block to `list_app_role_assigned_to` (key `grants:assigned_to:{sp}`), and either drop the cache from `list_app_role_assignments` or re-key it `grants:assignments:{sp}`; both mutator families already sweep the `grants:` prefix on Ok so invalidation is unchanged. Fix the doc comments to match. Add a wiremock test with `.expect(1)` on `/servicePrincipals/sp-graph/appRoleAssignedTo` called twice, and assert the existing `a_grant_write_invalidates_the_cached_matrices` shape for it.
verifier_notes: Premise verified. crates/azapptoolkit-graph/src/client/roles_grants.rs:36-65: `list_app_role_assignments` (path `/servicePrincipals/{id}/appRoleAssignments`) carries the read-through cache with key `assigned_to:{sp}` and a comment describing `prefetch_graph_app_roles` and the consent lens. roles_grants.rs:70-87: `list_app_role_assigned_to` (`/appRoleAssignedTo`) has the 'heaviest paged read' comment but ends with a bare `self.collect_all_pages(page).await` — no cache. Callers confirm the mismatch: audit.rs:957 and :1030, consent.rs:197, permission_tester.rs:467, enterprise_application.rs:190 all call `list_app_role_assigned_to`; `list_app_role_assignments` is called from 18 per-SP sites (permissions.rs:406/666/943, sharepoint.rs:307/543, exchange/*, remediation.rs:350, ...) including pre-write `existing` reads. docs/architecture/caching-and-search.md:284-287 names `appRoleAssignedTo` on the Graph SP as the dominating read. Tests: tests/grants.rs:244 and :270 only exercise `list_all_oauth2_grants`; the `grants:assigned_to:sp-1` key is hand-seeded in tests/service_principals.rs:650, so nothing pins which method writes it. History is squashed (all traces to merge 06af5cc) so no rationale for the current placement is recoverable. Proposal is sound: mutators already sweep the `grants:` prefix (roles_grants.rs:30-35), so moving the block changes no invalidation.

title: Advanced-query flag is inconsistent between page 1 and continuations: collect_all_pages defaults to eventual, the SP index does the reverse
rationale: Of the 12 `collect_all_pages` callers, only two (`list_service_principal_groups`, `list_tenant_app_role_resources`) issue page 1 with `ConsistencyLevel: eventual`; the other ten (owners, oauth2 grants, appRoleAssignedTo, federated credentials, managed identities, application templates, batch overflow continuations) issue page 1 without the header and every later page with it, so a multi-page collection is served half from the primary store and half from the eventually-consistent index. The SP index inverts it: `$count=true` + eventual on page 1, plain on pages 2+; per Microsoft's advanced-query doc the `$count=true` that rides the nextLink is then 'silently ignored', and `total_count` has no reader here anyway (the comment's justification — 'keeps the response shape identical to the prior index calls' — is not a functional reason; `list_application_index_named` already dropped `$count` for exactly the reasons applications.rs:244-249 lists). The transport's own history (transport.rs:307-316) shows page-1/page-2 header drift producing a silent wrong answer once already.
proposal: Delete the defaulted `collect_all_pages` wrapper (or default it to `false`) and make every call site pass the same flag it used for page 1 — mechanical, ten sites become `collect_all_pages_with(page, false)` and two become `true`. Drop `$count=true`/eventual from `list_service_principals_index` so page 1 matches its continuation (or, if there is a reason the index must be an advanced query, pass `true` to `collect_all_pages_capped` and document it). Add a wiremock regression for the transport.rs:307 bug: `list_applications_all` with `$expand` must have `header_is_missing("consistencylevel")` on the `page=2` mock — no test currently asserts that.
verifier_notes: Premise verified by enumerating callers. transport.rs:175-181 `collect_all_pages` hardcodes `collect_all_pages_with(page, true)`. Of its 12 callers, only directory.rs:174 (`list_service_principal_groups`) and service_principals.rs:149 (`list_tenant_app_role_resources`) issue page 1 with `true`; the other ten (applications.rs:387 owners, :573 templates via `get_json_prefer` which passes `false`, batch.rs:172 `finish_paged_batch`, credentials.rs:82 federated creds, roles_grants.rs:62/:85/:182/:202, service_principals.rs:118/:406) issue page 1 with `false` and then page with `eventual`. The SP index inverts it: service_principals.rs:168-183 sends `$count=true` + `eventual` on page 1 and `collect_all_pages_capped(page, SP_INDEX_MAX, false)` at :203-205; its stated reason (:161-164, 'keeps the response shape identical to the prior index calls') is not functional, and `total_count` is dropped (the fn returns `Vec<ServicePrincipal>`). Microsoft's paging doc (learn.microsoft.com/graph/paging, point 5; graph/query-parameters#skiptoken) states the ConsistencyLevel header 'isn't included by default in subsequent page requests. It must be set explicitly' for advanced queries — so the SP index's `false` continuation is the clearly wrong half, while the ten `false→true` sites read pages 2+ from the eventually-consistent index store, which can miss a just-written grant on a security-posture read. No test asserts the page-2 header: tests/applications.rs:365-405 `list_applications_all_follows_next_link` has no header matcher, and `header_is_missing("consistencylevel")` appears only on page-1 mocks (:37, :63). The transport's own history (transport.rs:307-316) shows this exact drift produced a silent wrong answer once. Proposal (drop the defaulted wrapper, pass the page-1 flag at every site) is mechanical and matches applications.rs:219-228's single-predicate rule.

title: Workspace tokio feature set is the union; library crates inherit net/io-util/rt-multi-thread/macros they don't use
rationale: Feature unification means the shipped binary is unaffected, so this is precision, not size: the manifests claim every client crate needs a multi-thread runtime and raw TCP, which is false and hides that the OAuth loopback listener is the single place raw sockets are opened — a fact worth being visible in a credential tool. It also slightly inflates `just test-crate <lib>` builds.
proposal: Set the workspace entry (Cargo.toml:26) to `features = ["sync", "time"]`. In crates/azapptoolkit-auth/Cargo.toml add `features = ["net", "io-util", "rt"]` — `rt` is required by the non-test `tokio::task::spawn_blocking` at service/mod.rs:457 and :509, not only the loopback listener — and add `[dev-dependencies] tokio = { workspace = true, features = ["macros", "rt"] }` (auth currently has no tokio dev-dep and its 7 `#[tokio::test]`s in loopback.rs and service/mod.rs ride the workspace `macros`/`rt-multi-thread`). In apps/desktop/src-tauri/Cargo.toml add `features = ["macros", "rt-multi-thread"]` (tokio::join! at enterprise_application.rs:131, backup.rs:368,519, readiness.rs:76, sso/mod.rs:466; tokio::spawn in five commands). graph/exchange/keyvault/arm/core already carry `macros`/`rt` dev-deps and use only tokio::sync/time in src.
verifier_notes: Premise verified: Cargo.toml:26 enables macros, rt-multi-thread, sync, time, net, io-util; only auth uses tokio::net/io (loopback.rs:7-8, service/mod.rs:34); no `Runtime::new`/`#[tokio::main]` anywhere (runtime is Tauri's); graph/exchange/keyvault/arm src use no tokio API beyond what tests need; core uses only tokio::time (http_retry.rs, cache). Overstated/incomplete: the proposal's auth feature set omits `rt`, which `spawn_blocking` (auth/service/mod.rs:457,509 — keyring I/O deliberately moved off the async worker) needs, and omits the dev-dependency auth would need for its `#[tokio::test]`s; as written the trim would break auth's build and tests. Value is precision only (feature unification leaves the shipped binary unchanged), so low.

title: reqwest http2 is off, so every Graph/Exchange fan-out multiplexes over HTTP/1.1 connections
evidence:
Cargo.toml:29:
reqwest = { version = "0.13", default-features = false, features = ["rustls", "json", "query", "form"] }

reqwest-0.13.5 default = ["default-tls", "charset", "http2", "system-proxy"] — `http2` is dropped by default-features = false and nothing re-enables it:
`cargo tree --locked -p desktop -e features -i reqwest` lists: __rustls, __rustls-aws-lc-rs, __tls, form, json, query, rustls, rustls-no-provider, stream, system-proxy (no http2).
`cargo tree -i h2 --target all` → "nothing to print" (h2 is not in the graph on any target).
rationale: Graph, Exchange Admin and Key Vault endpoints negotiate h2 via ALPN. With HTTP/1.1 only, a `ConcurrencyThrottle` fan-out at N in-flight requests holds N TLS connections per host; with h2 it multiplexes streams over one connection, cutting handshakes and connection-pool churn behind corporate proxies. Benefit is unmeasured here and `$batch` already reduces request count, so this is a measure-first item, not a defect.
proposal: Add `"http2"` to the workspace reqwest features (adds the `h2` crate), run an existing fan-out (e.g. the site sweep or audit on a large tenant) with `RUST_LOG=hyper_util=debug` before/after to count connections and wall time, keep it if it wins. Record the result next to the opt-level bench in Cargo.toml so it is not re-asked.
verifier_notes: Verified: Cargo.toml:29 omits `http2`; reqwest-0.13.5's `default = ["default-tls","charset","http2","system-proxy"]` is dropped by `default-features = false`; `cargo tree --locked --offline -p desktop -e features -i reqwest` lists no `reqwest feature "http2"` (only __rustls, __rustls-aws-lc-rs, __tls, form, json, query, rustls, rustls-no-provider, stream, system-proxy). Nuance on the h2 claim: with dev-deps included, `cargo tree -i h2` shows h2 ← hyper (feature "http2" via hyper "full"/hyper-util) ← hyper-rustls ← reqwest, which is why Cargo.lock:2033 contains h2; with `-e normal,build --target all` it is absent, so for the SHIPPED binary the reviewer's 'h2 not in the graph' and 'adds the h2 crate' both hold. No comment, doc or CHANGELOG entry records HTTP/1.1-only as deliberate (grep of Cargo.toml, docs/architecture). The finding is correctly framed as measure-first: `$batch` + ConcurrencyThrottle already bound request count, reqwest pools HTTP/1.1 keep-alive connections, and the auth crate already special-cases TLS-intercepting proxies (service/mod.rs:160,188) whose behaviour h2/ALPN can change — so the proposal to benchmark, decide, and record the result next to the opt-level bench is the right shape. Low, as stated.

title: create_application_core computes the initial secret lifetime without the 1..=730 clamp used by add_password
rationale: Three copies of the 180-day default and only one of the 1..=730 clamp. `initial_secret_lifetime_days: Option<u32>` accepts `Some(0)` (end == now, Graph 400, which then trips finding 1) and `Some(3650)` (a 10-year secret from a path whose sibling caps at 24 months). Today the create dialog never sends `initial_secret_*` (only bulk/restore reach the core, with `None`), so this is latent rather than live, but the seam is a public IPC argument.
proposal: Extract `clamp_secret_lifetime_days` (or make `resolve_password_window` pub(super)) in applications/credentials.rs and have `create_application_core` compute the end via it and call `add_password_window(&application.id, name, None, end)`. Leave `GraphClient::add_password` in place (keyvault/restore/sso still call it) or migrate those three callers in a separate change. One table test for 0 / 9999.
verifier_notes: Premise verified: mod.rs:354-356 `unwrap_or(180)` + `Duration::from_secs(days as u64 * 86_400)` with no clamp (0 and 3650 accepted), versus applications/credentials.rs:53 `MAX_SECRET_LIFETIME_DAYS = 730` and :81-82 `.clamp(1, ..)`; graph credentials.rs:38-39 has a third 180 default. Latent as stated: create_app_dialog.rs:44-55 never sets `initial_secret_*` and bulk.rs:566-570 / restore.rs:213-219 pass None. Overstated: 'delete `GraphClient::add_password` once callerless' — it has three other callers (keyvault.rs:94, restore.rs:594, sso/mod.rs:359), so it is not callerless after this change.

title: FanOutTicker::tick's doc claims count and cap are read under one lock — they are not — and progress events can arrive out of order
rationale: The cap is read after `drop(guard)`, and `current` is an atomic the mutex never protected anyway, so the comment describes a guarantee the code does not provide. Separately, every caller (`audit.rs:335-346`, bulk delete/grant/sweep) emits *after* `tick()` returns and outside any lock, so two tasks can tick 5 then 6 and emit 6 then 5; `use_progress_stream` (web-rs hooks) does `progress.set(Some(p))` unconditionally, so the bar can step backwards — the very skew the comment says is prevented. A `tokio::sync::Mutex<usize>` is also heavier than needed for a counter.
proposal: Replace `done: Arc<Mutex<usize>>` with `Arc<AtomicUsize>` and `fetch_add(1) + 1`; fix the comment to say the pair is best-effort. Make `use_progress_stream` (or a small `AuditProgress::newer_than`) ignore an event whose `done` is lower than the current one for the same `total`, so the bar is monotonic per run.
verifier_notes: throttle.rs:216-224: the doc says both values are read 'under the same lock acquisition', but the code does `drop(guard)` at :223 before `self.tracker.current_limit()` at :224, and `current` is an `AtomicUsize` (:33) the mutex never protected. Emission is outside any lock at every caller (audit.rs:335-346 ticks then emits; bulk.rs:250-258 likewise), so two tasks can tick 5,6 and emit 6,5; `use_progress_stream.rs:26-28` does `progress.set(Some(p))` unconditionally and neither security_view.rs nor bulk_action_bar.rs filters by `done`. Real but cosmetic (a one-step backward blip on a multi-threaded runtime), hence low. Proposal is fine; note `FanOutMeter::done()` (:190-192) is `async` today and would become sync with an atomic.

title: `use_debounced` leaks one `Closure::once_into_js` per cancelled timer (every keystroke that resets the debounce)
rationale: wasm-bindgen's `Closure::once_into_js` frees the Rust closure only when JS invokes it; a closure whose timer is cleared before firing is leaked for the life of the page. With a 300 ms debounce on every list filter, a fast typist cancels the pending timer on nearly every keystroke, leaking a boxed closure plus the captured `String` each time. Small per event, unbounded over a long session in a keep-alive app that never unmounts its lists. (`CopyIconButton` and `pairing.rs` also use `once_into_js`, but their timers always fire.)
proposal: Keep a `StoredValue<Option<Closure<dyn FnMut()>>, LocalStorage>` alongside the handle and drop it in `clear_pending` (dropping a `Closure` invalidates the JS side), or create one persistent `Closure` per hook instance that reads the latest value from `source.get_untracked()` when it fires.

title: CacheKind::idx is `self as usize` while the bucket array is sized by the hand-maintained ALL — a new variant compiles and panics with index-out-of-bounds on first use
rationale: The comment's claim is only half true: `ttl_for`'s exhaustive match forces a TTL arm, but a developer who adds `CacheKind::Foo`, a `ttl_for` arm and `record`/`CacheStats` arms gets a clean compile and a runtime panic (`index out of bounds: the len is 4 but the index is 4`) the first time `Foo` is read or written — inside a Tauri command, taking the request down. Nothing ties `ALL.len()` to the variant count.
proposal: Make `idx()` an exhaustive `match self { ServicePrincipal => 0, Permissions => 1, Audit => 2, Lists => 3 }` (so a new variant is a compile error here too) and add `const _: () = assert!(CacheKind::ALL.len() == CacheKind::Lists as usize + 1);` plus a unit test `for (i, k) in ALL.iter().enumerate() { assert_eq!(k.idx(), i) }`. Alternatively collapse `CacheStats`'s eight fields and `record` into `[Counters; ALL.len()]` indexed by `idx()`, removing two more hand-maintained tables.
verifier_notes: cache.rs:37-42 hand-lists `ALL: [CacheKind; 4]`, `idx()` (45-47) is `self as usize`, and `buckets: [Mutex<Bucket>; CacheKind::ALL.len()]` (366). The comment at 31-36 correctly notes `ttl_for` forces a new variant to be handled there (and `record` at 1108-1120 does too), but nothing forces `ALL` to grow: a fifth variant compiles and `buckets[4]` panics on first `get`/`put`. No test asserts `ALL[i].idx() == i` (grep). The proposal — exhaustive `match` in `idx()`, a `const` assert tying `ALL.len()` to the last discriminant + 1, and a small unit test — is cheap and idiomatic; collapsing `CacheStats` into `[Counters; ALL.len()]` is optional and would change the DTO shape diagnostics reads, so keep it separate. Low: latent, only bites on a future variant, but the failure mode is a runtime panic inside a Tauri command.

title: http_error_enum! consumers must carry an unnamed `thiserror` dependency — document it at the macro and in the manifests rather than trying to re-export it
rationale: Because the macro resolves `::thiserror` in the consumer's namespace, arm/graph/keyvault must each carry a dependency they never name in source. That makes cargo-machete (and any future reader) report three false positives, and a crate that adopts the macro later will fail to compile with a confusing "unresolved crate thiserror" error until it copies the dep. The standard fix is the `$crate` re-export idiom.
proposal: Keep `thiserror = { workspace = true }` in arm/graph/keyvault. Add one sentence to the http_error_enum! doc comment (core/src/http_error.rs ~:36) stating that a consumer crate must depend on `thiserror` directly because thiserror's derive expands hard-coded `::thiserror::__private` paths, and a one-line `# needed by core::http_error_enum!` comment beside each of the three manifest lines. If cargo-machete is adopted (finding 3), add `[package.metadata.cargo-machete] ignored = ["thiserror"]` to those three crates as a permanent, not temporary, entry.
verifier_notes: Premise true: crates/azapptoolkit-core/src/http_error.rs:65 derives `::thiserror::Error`, core/src/lib.rs has no thiserror re-export, and arm/graph/keyvault never name thiserror in source (only exchange does, error.rs:1). Proposal refuted on two counts. (1) 'core already depends on it' is false: crates/azapptoolkit-core/Cargo.toml:10-26 lists no thiserror (TokenError at core/src/token.rs:25 derives Debug/Clone/PartialEq/Eq with a manual Display at :57). (2) More importantly, the $crate re-export idiom does not work for thiserror: thiserror-impl's derive hard-codes absolute paths into the expansion — `::thiserror::#private::Var` (thiserror-impl-2.0.21/src/fmt.rs:149), `::thiserror::#private::Error` / `AsDynError` (expand.rs:39,43,49,67-68) — so even with `#[derive($crate::thiserror::Error)]` the generated code still resolves `::thiserror::__private` in the CONSUMER crate, and arm/graph/keyvault would fail to compile without their own direct dependency. The three manifests must keep thiserror.

title: http_error_enum! expands to ::thiserror::Error, so its three callers must declare thiserror with no textual use — undocumented in their manifests
rationale: Macro hygiene convention is `$crate::__private::dep` so the defining crate owns the dependency. Here the crate that owns the taxonomy does not declare thiserror while three callers must — and their manifests give no hint why (a grep of their src shows nothing using it). Any unused-dependency cleanup (manual or via cargo-machete, which this review recommends) removes those lines and the build fails inside a macro expansion with a confusing `::thiserror` path error.

Add the same note to the macro's doc comment in core/src/http_error.rs. Optionally add `thiserror = { workspace = true }` to core so the crate owning the taxonomy also declares it. If cargo-machete is adopted (finding [5]), add `[package.metadata.cargo-machete] ignored = ["thiserror"]` to the three callers.
verifier_notes: Premise verified: core/src/http_error.rs:65 `#[derive(Debug, ::thiserror::Error)]`, core's Cargo.toml has no thiserror, and graph/arm/keyvault (error.rs:10 each) declare it with no other use. But the proposed `$crate::thiserror::Error` re-export does NOT work: thiserror-impl 2.0.x's expansion hard-codes absolute `::thiserror::__private::...` paths in the generated code (registry thiserror-impl-2.0.18/src/expand.rs:212 `impl ... ::thiserror::#private::Error for #ty`, :68 `use ::thiserror::#private::AsDynError`, :39/:49 inferred bounds), and thiserror has no crate-path attribute (none in thiserror-impl/src/attr.rs). Since expansion happens in the caller's crate, each caller must have `thiserror` in its extern prelude regardless of how the derive is named — dropping the lines would fail exactly as the finding fears, and the refactor would too.     pub end_date_time: Option<String>,
crates/azapptoolkit-dto/src/audit.rs:564  pub completed_at: Option<String>,   (doc: "RFC3339 UTC")
crates/azapptoolkit-dto/src/applications.rs:247  pub expires: String,   (doc: "RFC3339 certificate expiry")
vs

    pub start_date_time: Option<DateTime<Utc>>,

title: list_conditional_access_policies pages without $top, contrary to the 'every paged read sends $top' invariant

        &self,
        token: &Arc<dyn BearerProvider>,
        method: Method,
        url: &str,
        body: &B,

        B: Serialize + ?Sized,

rationale: Tauri `#[tauri::command] async fn`s must return Send futures, so today every call compiles only because each concrete body type happens to be Sync. Tauri async commands must produce Send futures, so the premise about where a non-Sync body would fail (inside generate_handler!, opaquely) holds.
